preface: The book is one reference written from the owner's 69 collected artifacts and the SchwingNet repository's own research notes, for whoever plans the next experiment. It is organised in seven parts in reading order, Orientation, Data, Methods, Evaluation, Operations, the Decision log, and Open questions with the ranked backlog, followed by a part labelled separable, Part S, which holds the Symphony and Beethoven material alone (the protocol and its origins, the Claude workers on the grid, the Beethoven repositories, roadmap and store release, the workstation runbook and the Claude-on-Slurm playbook) so it can be split out without touching the rest; Part V keeps only the operations a SchwingNet experiment needs. Chapter files are numbered 01 to 32 across the parts under docs/textbook/, ASCII and LF, each 2,000 to 6,000 words of prose. Every chapter follows one template: a purpose paragraph that says what it settles for a planner; the body, built from the canonical artifacts of its cluster with each superseded or duplicate artifact named and what that older version alone still holds; then four closing sections, 'What we know', 'What we do not know', 'What would change our mind', and a provenance table that maps each statement to the artifact or repository file it comes from and an evidence grade, and may give the artifact's claude.ai link beside its repository path, as the owner allowed on 2026-10-23, saying the artifacts are shared with anyone who has the link. The grades are Measured (a number read from a result file or computed by tested code on held-out data, with its n and interval), Reported (stated by an artifact or a paper without the file behind it being read), Inferred (a judgment the artifacts draw from measurements, or a design claim, with no outcome measured) and Unverified (asserted with no source, or contradicted by another record); the artifacts' own grades map onto these, Verified to Measured and Open to Unverified. A headline number from a superseded or leaked family, such as allspine v2's 99.02 percent, may be quoted as a record and never as a final value: with a direct link to the file or artifact it comes from, so that it can be updated automatically later, and a disclaimer that it is not a final value. That is the owner's answer of 2026-10-23, which revises for the book the decision recorded in the handoff of 2026-10-08 that these families' numbers are never quoted; where the contradictions page says a figure must be run again before it is quoted, that holds for quoting it as a current value. Confidential method material (what each stage does and the method decisions) sits only in Part III, whose chapters are marked confidential-method; results may be shown, mechanism may not, until the provisional is filed. People appear by role only, and no e-mail address, phone number or home address is reproduced anywhere.

chapters.title: The goal and the constraints
chapters.purpose: Settles what SchwingNet is for (naming the vertebral level from what the surgeon has in the room, on the hospital's own C-arm), why wrong-level surgery is the problem it answers, which two lines of work exist (counting from an anchor and naming from morphology) and the hard constraints every experiment runs under: confidentiality until the provisional is filed, no grid job or training without the owner's word and a number, no usage credits, the private-forever list, the IRB umbrella and the schedule to the provisional (30 October) and the CNS talk (2 November 2026). It names the two lines without giving their mechanism, which is Part III's.
questions_answered: What does the project make, for whom, and what does done look like?
Why is wrong-level surgery framed as a counting problem, and what do the registry, survey and cost figures say?
Which constraints bind every experiment (confidentiality, the owner's word, credits, public release, the IRB umbrella, the private-forever list)?
What is the calendar to the provisional and the talk, and what drops first if time runs short?
chapters.research_needed: Check the wrong-level figures (0.12 percent of 34,544 registry operations, 81.3 percent intraoperative disorientation, the survey and indemnity figures) against the cited registry and survey papers; confirm the IRB umbrella number and its five criteria against the determination letter the owner holds; confirm the provisional and talk dates against docs/project.md and the retraining plan.

chapters.title: Counting from an anchor along a sweep
chapters.purpose: States the counting line as the 22 September report and the manuscript figures hold it: expose at the anchor (sacrum or C2), detect bodies and the anchor, link overlapping frames by normalised cross-correlation within 0.6 of a body of the commanded step, chain, count k from the anchor, confirm with the instrument on bone; no name formed; refusal rather than a guess when a frame fails to link. It gives the R + C = 22 rule and its limits, the twelve-arm exactness, the sweep protocol (a 9-inch field, two bodies of overlap, four vertebrae in frame on a thoracolumbar-variant spine), the audit of the synthetic pipeline (device cards sampling fitted distributions), what the two figure builds of that evening hold and which rows are not quotable (the verse_drr spacing), and the known failure modes (detection, the anchor missed, a lumbarised S1, the counting error compounding over the column).

chapters.title: Naming from morphology, context and a sweep

chapters.title: Renders, physics and the sim-to-real gap
chapters.purpose: States where training frames come from and why the CT-to-fluoroscopy map is calibrated rather than learned: the render corpora and their resolution (93 px for a 140 mm field, which the film ladder shows costs nothing), DeepFluoro as the calibration set (physics explains 80.9 percent of attenuation variance, nine device terms add 4.3 points, boxed scatter), what is left after physics on four frames (the twelve-coefficient smooth field is most of the gap; the 2 to 16 px bands two to seven times the noise floor, so 'nothing local' was withdrawn), the verdicts on lifting to 3-D (do not build a reconstruction stage), registration as a label source (registered real frames beat their DRR twins), synthetic editing (hardware yes, transitional editing worth a week, no whole-CT generation), and the refuted routes (GAN, FluoroGen img2img, CUT v1, super-resolution). It records what the 21 September board alone holds (the resolution ladder, eight domain-randomisation arms, the void C2 arm).

chapters.title: Transitional anatomy: two anchors, disagreement and abstention

It lists every mechanism tried with its measured result and the stop rules that gate the next arms.

chapters.title: SchwingCheck: an explainable Bayesian check on vertebral labels
chapters.purpose: Carries the owner's white paper on SchwingCheck whole, at revision 188, with five diagrams drawn for it: SchwingNet's stages as built and where SchwingCheck joins them; the rule that names the bodies in view from seven measurements an anatomist would recognise and returns a probability over every place between C3 and L5; the paper's three pathways to a level label, LevelCheck as prior art, SchwingCheck3D with a preoperative CT and SchwingCheck2D without one; the seven measures as distances between landmarks; and a proposed device that reads them in one landmark pass with no segmentation, to keep the latency low. Every SchwingCheck number is from synthetic columns drawn from Panjabi's tables.

notes: Thirty-two chapters: Part I 3, Part II 6, Part III 7, Part IV 4, Part V 3, Part VI 3, Part VII 2, Part S 4. Every one of the 69 artifact ids has at least one chapter, checked by script; each superseded artifact (schwingnet-figures-jshksq, vertebral-levels-without-ct-a4rydj, spine-x-ray-data-handoff-bddbdd, fluorocap-corpus-audit-9hjzzs, openspine-board-t3gfds, ninety-three-pixels, protocol-1-eprotocol-draft-mkmh7p, shared-multi-account-claude-project-plan-rqzwh9, celebrate-life-flyer-noutom) is placed in the chapter that uses its canonical version, with the chapter's purpose naming what the older page alone holds. The settled clustering's fourteen clusters map onto chapters as follows: level naming and counting into chapters 10 and 11 (the counting and naming lines kept as two chapters because a planner must choose between the targets, with chapter 16 holding how they coexist); transitional vertebrae into chapter 14 with the dataset-level findings (rib audit, border variants) in chapter 7; datasets and holdings into chapters 4 to 7 and 9; FluoroCap into chapter 8 (data) and chapter 15 (decoder and model); verification benches and readiness audits into chapters 17 and 20 with the OR ledger also feeding chapters 12 and 19; detectors and architecture into chapter 12; renders and physics into chapter 13; the OR case (proposal, grant, IRB drafts) into chapter 20; programme direction and handoffs into chapters 1, 3, 23, 25, 27 and 28; the four symphony-beethoven clusters into chapters 29 to 32; outreach into chapter 26.
